title: 雁门太守行
titleEn: Song of the Governor of Yanmen
author: 李贺
intro: Black clouds crush down on a besieged city, armour flashes like golden scales, the sky turns rouge and purple at dusk — a battle painted almost entirely in colour, ending with soldiers ready to die for their ruler.
analysis: 这首诗写一场边塞守城战，最大的特点是用浓烈的颜色来写战争。第一句写敌军像黑云一样压过来，城好像要被压塌了；守城将士的铠甲在阳光下闪闪发光，像金色的鱼鳞。接着写号角声响满秋天的天空，边塞的泥土在暮色里凝成胭脂一样的紫红色——暗示战场上的血。第三联写援军半卷着红旗赶到易水边，夜里霜很重，战鼓都被冻得敲不响了。最后两句说：为了报答君王的重用，我们愿意手提宝剑为他战死。黑、金、紫、红、白（霜）交错在一起，画面感极强。“黑云压城城欲摧”今天常用来形容形势紧张、压力很大。
analysisEn: This poem describes the defence of a frontier city, and what makes it unforgettable is colour. The enemy arrives like black clouds pressing down until the city walls seem about to crack; the defenders’ armour catches the sun and opens like golden fish scales. Bugle calls fill the autumn sky, and at dusk the frontier earth sets into a rouge-purple — a hint of the blood spilled there. Then reinforcements reach the Yi River with their red banners half furled; the frost lies so heavy that the cold drums will barely sound. In the last couplet the soldiers declare that, to repay their ruler’s trust, they will take up their “jade dragons” — their swords — and die for him. Black, gold, purple, red and the white of frost flash one after another, like scenes in a film. Notice, too, that Li He hardly describes the fighting itself: we see only the sky, the armour, the earth, the banners and the drums, and imagine the rest. The opening line, 黑云压城城欲摧, is still used today for any tense moment when pressure seems overwhelming.
background: Li He (790–816), a descendant of the Tang royal house, was famous for his dazzling, strange imagery and died at 26. Tradition says that when he showed this poem to the great writer Han Yu, Han Yu was so struck by the first two lines that he hurried to meet him.
pronunciation: 多音字：燕脂 yān（同“胭脂”，不读 yàn）；角声 jiǎo（号角）；塞上 sài；半卷 juǎn；霜重 zhòng；为君死 wèi。易水 yì。
version: 采用统编教材版本。“甲光向日”一作“向月”；“燕脂”一作“胭脂”，意思相同。

lines.py: hēi yún yā chéng chéng yù cuī
lines.lit: Black clouds press on the city; the city is about to crumble;
lines.en: Black clouds bear down until the walls seem ready to crack;

lines.py: jiǎ guāng xiàng rì jīn lín kāi
lines.lit: armour gleams toward the sun, opening like golden scales.
lines.en: armour flashes in the sun like opening golden scales.

lines.py: jiǎo shēng mǎn tiān qiū sè lǐ
lines.lit: Bugle sounds fill the sky in the autumn colours;
lines.en: Bugles fill the whole autumn sky,

lines.py: sài shàng yān zhī níng yè zǐ
lines.lit: on the frontier, rouge-red earth sets into night purple.
lines.en: and the rouge-red frontier earth darkens to purple at nightfall.

lines.py: bàn juǎn hóng qí lín yì shuǐ
lines.lit: Red banners half furled, they reach the Yi River;
lines.en: Red banners half furled, they come to the Yi River;

lines.py: shuāng zhòng gǔ hán shēng bù qǐ
lines.lit: frost is heavy, drums are cold, their sound will not rise.
lines.en: the frost lies thick, and the frozen drums will hardly sound.

lines.py: bào jūn huáng jīn tái shàng yì
lines.lit: To repay the lord’s favour shown at the Golden Terrace,
lines.en: To repay the trust our lord placed in us,

lines.py: tí xié yù lóng wèi jūn sǐ
lines.lit: we take up our jade dragons and die for the lord.
lines.en: we take up our swords and die for him.

words.note: 古代地方长官，现代汉语不用。
古诗体的一种，如《琵琶行》。
现代汉语有“摧毁”“无坚不摧”。
荆轲刺秦王前在这里告别，带有悲壮色彩。
战国时燕昭王筑台放黄金，招揽天下人才；比喻君王重用人才。
古义是“拿着”；今天“提携”指帮助、提拔后辈。
诗里的借代说法，现代汉语不用。

imagery.name: 云
imagery.zh: 黑云比喻来势汹汹的敌军，压得城池快要倒塌。
imagery.en: Black clouds stand for the enemy army bearing down until the city seems ready to fall.

imagery.name: 霜
imagery.zh: 浓霜写出夜里的严寒，也写出战斗的艰苦。
imagery.en: Heavy frost shows the bitter night cold and how hard the fighting is.

imagery.name: 鼓
imagery.zh: 战鼓冻得敲不响，暗示形势危急、将士处境艰难。
imagery.en: Drums too frozen to sound hint at a desperate situation.

imagery.name: 台
imagery.zh: 黄金台代表君王对人才的重用，将士以死相报。
imagery.en: The Golden Terrace stands for a ruler who values talent — and the soldiers repay it with their lives.

imagery.name: 剑
imagery.zh: “玉龙”指宝剑，表示将士手握兵器、誓死报国的决心。
imagery.en: The “jade dragon” is a sword: the soldiers grip it, ready to die for their country.
